verdict: The 4.4x cold-blackbody asymmetry in Search T is the CMB. Three independent lines agree. The fitted temperature of the cold tail peaks at 2.75 K, the grid point nearest T_CMB = 2.72548 K, with 66% of the tail inside 0.5 K of it, although T was free over 2-40 K. The classification rate rises 56x from the Galactic plane to the pole, which is the signature of a fixed-amplitude isotropic field competing against a Galactic foreground, while the mirror tail instead tracks the catalogue and is disc-like. And the asymmetry vanishes under every cut that removes CMB confusion: at T >= 4 K the ratio falls from 4.39 to 0.40 (88 cold against 220 mirror, so the cold side sits BELOW its own false-positive rate), and restricting to |b| < 10 deg alone brings it to 0.93. RESULT: null at T >= 4 K, with excess over mirror <= 0. COVERAGE GAP, stated rather than implied: the 2.5-3.5 K window is spectrally degenerate with CMB anisotropy in Planck broadband photometry and this channel sets no limit there. That degeneracy is the same one the channel was built on -- a cold radiator survives component separation because it looks like a CMB fluctuation, which necessarily means CMB fluctuations look like it. Breaking it requires angular profile, millimetre follow-up at ACT or SPT resolution, or the non-Gaussianity of a discrete population against a Gaussian field.
